lines.text: אַחְלָמָה f. Ex. 28, 19, the name of a
gem, Sept. Vulg. ἀμέθυστος, amethyst;
but Josephus gives it by ἀχάτης, agate,
though there seems to be some confusion
in the order of his words. The form is
that of a verbal of Hiph. from r. חָלַם to
dream; perhaps because it was worn as
an amulet to induce dreams. A similar
superstition is also the ground of the
name ἀμέθυστος, this stone being re-
garded as a charm against drunkenness.
Comp. Braun de Vestitu sacerdot. Heb.
אַחְמְתָא Ezra 6, 2, Achmetha, i. e.
Ecbatana, the ancient metropolis of
Media, the summer residence of the Per-
sian kings. The ancient orthography
of this name is traced by Lassen (Ind.
Biblioth. III. 36) in the Sanscr. açva-
dhana, i. e. ἱπποστασία; the Sanscr. ç
passing over sometimes into a guttural
and sometimes into s. The correspond-
ing modern name is Ispahan.
אֲחַסְבַּי pr. n. m. Ahasbai, 2 Sam. 23,
34. From אֶחְסֶה בְיָהּ I take refuge in
Jehovah.
* אָחַר to be after, behind; to stay be-
hind; hence, to stay, to delay, to remain,
in Kal once, 1 pers. fut. וָאֵחַר Gen. 32,5.—
Arab. أَخَّرَ Conj. II, to defer, to delay.
Syr. Aph. and Shaph. ܐܰܘܚܰܪ and ܫܰܘܚܰܪ
id.
Piel אֵחַר, plur. אֵחֲרוּ for אִחֲרוּ Judg.
5, 28, fut. יְאַחֵר.
1. to delay, to retard, to hinder any
one, Gen. 24, 56; to delay, to defer any
thing Ex. 22, 28. Also ellipt. Deut. 7,
10 he will not delay (punishment) to
him who hateth him.
2. Intrans. i. q. Kal, to stay, to delay,
to linger. Judg. 4, 28 why linger the
paces of his chariots? Ps. 40, 18 אַל־
תְּאַחַר delay not. 70, 6. Gen. 34, 19.
3. to stay long, to tarry late in or by
any thing, with עַל, Prov. 23, 30 מְאַחֲרִים
עַל הַיַּיִן who tarry long at the wine, i. e.
who drink till late in the night. Comp.
Deriv. אַחַר—אֲחֹרַנִּית, and אָחוֹר.
אַחֵר (Dag. forte impl.) f. אַחֶרֶת, Plur.
אֲחֵרִים, אֲחֵרוֹת, from an obsol. sing. אָחֵר
with Kamets pure.
1. Adj. pr. after, hinder, following
spec. next following, next, second, (comp.
secundus a sequendo,) Gen. 17, 21 בַּשָּׁנָה
הָאַחֶרֶת in the next year, the following
year. 1 K. 3, 22.—Hence genr. another,
other; alius, alia, aliud; Gen. 4, 25. 8
10. 12. 29, 19. al. sæp. Arab. آخَرُ id.
Syr. ܐ݈ܚܪܺܝܢ, ܐ݈ܚܪܺܢܳܐ, plur. ܐ݈ܚܪ̈ܳܢܶܐ, Chald.
אָחֳרָן.—So אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים other gods,
i. e. idols, Deut. 6, 14. 7, 4. Jer. 1, 16.
7, 18. al. sæp. Sing. אֵל אַחֵר Ex. 34, 14;
without אֵל id. Is. 42, 8 וּכְבוֹדִי לְאַחֵר לֹא־
אֶתֵּן and my glory will I not give unto
another god. 48, 11. Ps. 16, 4 אַחֵר (אֲשֶׁר)
מָהָרוּ who hasten to another god, i. e.
away from the true God after idols.
2. Aher, pr. n. m. 1 Chr. 7, 12.
אַחַר pr. after, the after part, hinder
part, extremity. Hence
1. Adv. a) Of place, behind, in the
back-ground. Gen. 22, 13 וְהִנֵּה אַיִל אַחַר
נֶאֱחַז בַּסְּבַךְ בְּקַרְנָיו and lo! a ram in the
back-ground, caught in a thicket by his
horns. Abraham did not see the ram
behind himself, as the Vulgate renders,
and as it is usually taken; but in the
distant part, the back-ground, of what
lay before his eyes. [Yet he may
naturally be supposed to have looked
round on hearing the angel’s voice.—T.]
Nor is it necessary to read אֶחָד, with
the Samar. Sept. Syr. and 42 Mss. b)
Adv. of time, afterwards, then, Gen. 10,
2. Prep. a) Of place, behind, Cant.
2, 9. Ex. 3, 1 behind the desert, back of
it, i. e. on the west of the desert, see in
אָחוֹר no. 2. Also after, as הָלַךְ אַחַר פ׳
to go after, to follow any one, Gen. 37, 17.
Job 31, 7. מֵאַחַר prægn. pr. from after,
Ps. 78, 71 מֵאַחַר עָלוֹת הֱבִיאוֹ from after
the ewes he brought him, i. e. from fol-
lowing the ewes, from being a shep-
herd. b) Prep. of time, after, Gen. 9,
28. So אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה after these
things, i. e. afterwards, a formula of
transition, Gen. 15, 1. 22, 1. With infin.
after that, after, Num. 6, 19. אַחַר כֵּן
pr. after so, i. e. after it had so hap-
pened, afterwards, Lev. 14, 36. Deut.
3. Conj. אַחַר אֲשֶׁר after that, Ez. 40, 1;
and without אֲשֶׁר, Lev. 14, 43. Job 42, 7.

line_status.note: The bet of בְיָהּ is printed without a dagesh (only sheva beneath); Reading A's dagesh in בְּ is not on the page. The rest of the line is identical in both readings and matches the print.

The vowel signs over alaph/shin and heth are printed as angled West Syriac pthaha strokes (U+0730), not the two-dot East Syriac pthaha (U+0731) of Reading B; consonants and order are identical in both readings.
The first aleph carries tsere (two dots, matching the plural אֵחֲרוּ), not hireq; only the third word אִחֲרוּ has the single hireq dot.

Under the first yod of הַיַּיִן the print shows a flat patach (plus dagesh in the yod), not a qamets with a descending tail; Reading A's יָּ is wrong. The rest of the line is identical in both readings.

The only difference is spacing around the em dash; in print the dash is set tight against both Hebrew words (no spaces), as in B. All vowels, the dagesh in nun, and plene אָחוֹר agree in both readings and match the print.

Second word: the letter before final alaph is the same looped nun as in the plural (ܢܳܐ), not taw — so B's feminine ܐܚܪܺܬ݂ܳܐ is wrong; but the vowel over its rish is the same "=" ḥbasa sign as in word 1, not zqapha as in A. All three words carry a printed line under the alaph (linea occultans, written here as U+0748 below, not B's U+0747 above). No rukkakha dot is printed.
